What Is Dual Diagnosis?

Dual diagnosis, also known as co-occurring disorders, refers to when a person experiences both a substance use disorder and a mental health condition at the same time. Common examples include struggling with addiction and depression, anxiety and alcohol dependence, or PTSD and drug use.

These conditions often interact. Substance use can worsen mental health symptoms, while untreated mental illness can make recovery more difficult. That’s why dual diagnosis treatment is essential: it addresses both issues together through a coordinated, evidence-based approach.

At Marina Harbor Detox, our clinical team evaluates each client’s mental and physical health to create an individualized plan that treats the whole person, not just the symptoms. By focusing on both addiction and mental health recovery, we help clients achieve lasting healing.
What to expect in our Dual Diagnosis Program

At Marina Harbor Detox, we understand that addiction and mental health challenges often go hand in hand. Our dual diagnosis treatment program provides integrated care for individuals facing both substance use disorders and underlying mental health conditions such as anxiety, depression, or trauma.

By addressing both conditions at the same time, we help clients uncover the root causes of addiction, develop healthier coping strategies, and build a foundation for lasting recovery. Our Integrated Approach Includes:
Medical Detox & Stabilization – Safe, supervised detoxification for a strong start to recovery.
Mental Health Assessment – Comprehensive evaluation to identify co-occurring disorders.
Individual & Group Therapy – Evidence-based sessions that promote understanding and emotional growth.
Medication Management – When appropriate, medications are used to help balance mood and reduce symptoms.
Aftercare Planning – Ongoing support and referrals for continued treatment once detox is complete.
